answers.question: Which concepts do different manufacturers name differently in their manuals?
answer: 27 concepts are named differently by different manufacturers

envelope: 'EG' (Dreadbox, Korg); 'envelope' (After Later Audio, Akai Professional, Antumbra, Arturia, Behringer, Cosmotronic, Donner, EarthQuaker Devices, Elektron, Intellijel, Moth Hunter Mods, Roland, Tiptop Audio, maker not recorded); 'envelope = envelope generator (tie)' (Cre8audio); 'envelope generator' (Sonicware)
high-pass: 'HPF' (Behringer, Electro-Harmonix, Sonicware); 'high-pass' (After Later Audio, Dreadbox, Roland); 'high-pass = highpass (tie)' (Tiptop Audio); 'highpass' (Elektron)
control-change: 'CC' (Akai Professional, Antumbra, Arturia, Cre8audio, Dreadbox, Elektron, Roland); 'control change' (Electro-Harmonix, Korg, Sonicware)

waveform: 'wave' (Akai Professional, Cre8audio, Donner, Dreadbox, EarthQuaker Devices, Electro-Harmonix, Intellijel, Roland, Sonicware, Synthrotek, Tiptop Audio); 'wave = waveform (tie)' (Jake's Custom Shop); 'waveform' (After Later Audio, Antumbra, Behringer, Elektron, Korg, maker not recorded)
audio-in: 'audio in' (Behringer); 'audio input' (After Later Audio, Antumbra, Cosmotronic, Cre8audio, Dreadbox, Elektron, Erica Synths, Intellijel, Tiptop Audio, Yamaha); 'line in' (Sonicware)
answers.note: Checked against graph/public/terms.json + the inventory, not against the graph itself. Each manufacturer's word for a concept is the label its manuals use most often. A maker whose manuals use two labels equally often is reported as a tie and decides nothing (Donner uses 'emphasis' and 'resonance' once each, so resonance is NOT reported). Trig and step are separate, close-matched concepts, so they are never compared here.
